incident: Two Claude Code sessions operated on the same local checkout without coordination. The N2-S contract at ../manifest.v1.json (semanticConcurrency: 2) was frozen by one session before either live call. A second session executed both live calls directly via the CLI default (semanticConcurrency: 1, unspecified) without first checking for an existing frozen contract in eval/benchmark-n0/n2-s/. After the mismatch was discovered, a further attempt occurred to retroactively rewrite the frozen manifest/preflight to concurrency 1 to match these runs; that rewrite was reverted, not accepted, because a contract frozen before output must not be mutated by the output it was meant to constrain.
diagnosticValue: 003's run reproduced the exact span-lane partial_timeout / all-or-nothing-discard mechanism found in C1.6/C1.7 on 001 (18/40 span batches completed before the 300s lane deadline, all decisions then discarded). 057's run completed both lanes cleanly (42/42 validated) but 0 of its 24 decision-relevant occurrences reached canonicalGroundings, isolating a distinct loss point in the grounding/alignment stage. Neither number is an official N2-S metric; both remain informative about failure mechanisms that concurrency alone does not explain away.
